questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few lockers are cheques. All cheques are accounts. No accounts is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some lockers are not cheques.
II. No cheques is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some lockers are cheques. All cheques are accounts. No accounts is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some lockers are accounts.
II. Some cheques are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few lockers are cheques. Some cheques are accounts. All accounts are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All lockers are bonds.
II. No cheques is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No lockers is a cheques. Some cheques are accounts. All accounts are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All lockers are bonds.
II. Some bonds are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: S = T = P < U > X.
Conclusions: I. U < P   II. T ≤ X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: V < Q = T > S < X.
Conclusions: I. Q ≥ S   II. X ≤ T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: R < V > U < Q < X.
Conclusions: I. X > V   II. Q ≤ V.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
growth banking digital = su vo pa
growth rural savings = ka vo ni
banking rural access = pa ni ze
digital savings access = su ka ze
growth banking access = vo ze pa
What is the code for “savings”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ka. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: growth = vo, banking = pa, digital = su, rural = ni, savings = ka, access = ze.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 46 km east, turns left and walks 52 km, then turns left and walks 7 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 65. Net displacement is 39 km east and 52 km north. By Pythagoras, √(39² + 52²) = 65 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 26 km east, turns left and walks 32 km, then turns left and walks 2 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. Net displacement is 24 km east and 32 km north. By Pythagoras, √(24² + 32²) = 40 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 22 km east, turns left and walks 8 km, then turns left and walks 16 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 10. Net displacement is 6 km east and 8 km north. By Pythagoras, √(6² + 8²) = 10 km.

questions.stem: F is the mother of B. H is the son of B. A is the father of B. How is H related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. A is a parent of B, and H is B’s son. Hence H is A’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of E. E is the mother of G. F is the father of A and E. How is A related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of G’s mother E. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A is the only daughter of B. B is the father of A. D is the son of A. C is the sister of B. How is B related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. B is the father of A, and A is D’s mother. Thus B is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 59 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. New front rank = 21+3 = 24. Back rank = 59 − 24 + 1 = 36.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. New front rank = 21+4 = 25. Back rank = 64 − 25 + 1 = 40.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1050. It is marked above cost and sold at a 20% discount on marked price, earning 25% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 1640.62. Selling price = 1050 × 125/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.8 = 1640.62.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 18 days and B in 27 days. They work together for 3 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need?
questions.explanation: Answer: 13. Use 54 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 54 − 3×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹11000 at 5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)

questions.stem: A vessel contains 85 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 17. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 17.

questions.stem: The average of 19 numbers is 45. One number, 57, is replaced and the average rises by 6. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 171. Total increases by 19 × 6. New number = 57 + 114.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 4 years, their combined age will be 88 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 8 = 88; x = 20, so father = 60.
